evidence.claim: Putin authorized the full-scale invasion of Ukraine and said the goal was to demilitarise and 'denazify' Ukraine.
evidence.title: Russia's Putin authorises 'special military operation' against Ukraine
evidence.excerpt: Putin authorized the full-scale invasion of Ukraine and said the goal was to demilitarise and 'denazify' Ukraine.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters report quoting the president directly on the launch decision and justification.
contrary_evidence: The Kremlin framed the operation as defensive.
The report shows the operational choice was still an invasion.

evidence.claim: Rosstat said Russia's economy contracted by 1.2% in 2022, and Reuters noted that Western sanctions followed Putin's decision to send troops into Ukraine.
evidence.title: Russian economy shrank by 1.2% in 2022, less than previously thought - stats service
evidence.excerpt: Rosstat said Russia's economy contracted by 1.2% in 2022, and Reuters noted that Western sanctions followed Putin's decision to send troops into Ukraine.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters report of the official statistics-service revision; strong for the final 2022 GDP figure.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective on the 2022 target-year GDP outcome.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong on overall outcome attribution: the contraction is explicitly linked to Putin's invasion decision, though later revisions and wartime spending complicate exact magnitude.
contrary_evidence: The final contraction was smaller than earlier estimates, so the immediate collapse was limited.
War spending later supported measured growth, but that does not change the 2022 loss in civilian prosperity.

evidence.claim: Putin said the operation's goal was to protect people in Donbas and to demilitarise and denazify Ukraine, making the war's core aim explicit.
evidence.title: Russia's Putin authorises 'special military operation' against Ukraine
evidence.excerpt: Putin said the operation's goal was to protect people in Donbas and to demilitarise and denazify Ukraine, making the war's core aim explicit.
evidence.source_locator: Reuters lead paragraph / quoted address in search result snippet
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting on Putin's own televised announcement; direct quote and immediate publication date match the target period.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the 2022 target period and program origin point.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct and strong; this is Putin's own public statement, though self-justifying and contested by Ukraine and Western governments.
contrary_evidence: Ukraine and Western officials characterized the invasion as an imperialist war, not a protective operation.

evidence.claim: Moscow signalled it was scaling back its ambitions in Ukraine to focus on Donbass, saying the first phase was mostly complete and that the main goal was the 'liberation of Donbass'.
evidence.title: Russia reframes war goals as Ukrainians advance near Kyiv
evidence.excerpt: Moscow signalled it was scaling back its ambitions in Ukraine to focus on Donbass, saying the first phase was mostly complete and that the main goal was the 'liberation of Donbass'.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting with a precise date and a concrete statement by the Russian defence ministry during the 2022 campaign.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and squarely about execution of the war program.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong but indirect; the statement came from the Russian defence ministry under Putin's rule and was used to justify a course correction after setbacks.
contrary_evidence: The same report says Russian troops had failed to capture any major city in the first month and were being pushed back near Kyiv.

evidence.claim: Putin ordered Russia's first mobilisation since World War Two after a major battlefield reversal, with Shoigu saying 300,000 reservists would be drafted to support the war in Ukraine.
evidence.title: Russia calls up 300,000 reservists, says 6,000 soldiers killed in Ukraine
evidence.excerpt: Putin ordered Russia's first mobilisation since World War Two after a major battlefield reversal, with Shoigu saying 300,000 reservists would be drafted to support the war in Ukraine.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on a major 2022 strategic decision and its immediate implementation parameters.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the target year and a central adaptation point.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong; the mobilisation followed Putin's order and was part of the state response to battlefield reversals under his command.
contrary_evidence: The same story reports heavy casualties and frames the mobilisation as a response to setbacks rather than evidence of prior success.

evidence.claim: Russia exempted some bankers, IT workers and journalists from mobilisation in order to keep critical industries and the financial system functioning smoothly.
evidence.title: Russia excludes some IT professionals, bankers and journalists from mobilisation
evidence.excerpt: Russia exempted some bankers, IT workers and journalists from mobilisation in order to keep critical industries and the financial system functioning smoothly.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reports an explicit policy exception with stated operational rationale from the central bank and defence ministry.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the target year and part of wartime implementation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to Putin's governing network, though the measure is implemented by ministries and the central bank rather than Putin personally.
contrary_evidence: The exemptions also reveal that mobilisation was causing practical strain and required improvisation.

evidence.claim: Russia's Defence Ministry named Sergei Surovikin overall commander of forces fighting in Ukraine after a series of dramatic reverses, as part of an effort to centralise command and control.
evidence.title: Russia names air force general to lead its forces in Ukraine
evidence.excerpt: Russia's Defence Ministry named Sergei Surovikin overall commander of forces fighting in Ukraine after a series of dramatic reverses, as part of an effort to centralise command and control.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters coverage of a major command reshuffle with explicit mention of the operational rationale.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and clearly part of wartime adaptation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong; the command change occurred under Putin's war leadership, though the ministerial chain executed it.
contrary_evidence: Command changes can indicate failure as well as adaptation; the appointment does not itself prove improved battlefield performance.

evidence.claim: Russia said it had completed its withdrawal from Kherson, a lightning-fast retreat of tens of thousands of troops that Reuters described as a major setback and the loss of the only regional capital Russia captured after the invasion.
evidence.title: Russia says it has completed retreat from Kherson
evidence.excerpt: Russia said it had completed its withdrawal from Kherson, a lightning-fast retreat of tens of thousands of troops that Reuters described as a major setback and the loss of the only regional capital Russia captured after the invasion.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters report with clear attribution and detailed battlefield consequences; the article provides a strong negative outcome marker for the war program.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and decisive for end-of-year war performance.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong; the withdrawal was ordered by Russia's defence ministry under Putin's overall war authority, though Surovikin and Shoigu handled the immediate decision.
contrary_evidence: Russian officials framed the move as an orderly transfer to defensive lines and said they were still committed to the operation's goals.

evidence.claim: Putin told defence-industry chiefs that the key task was to provide frontline units with weapons, equipment, ammunition and gear in the necessary quantities and shortest timeframes.
evidence.title: Putin tells Russian defence industry to up its game for Ukraine war
evidence.excerpt: Putin told defence-industry chiefs that the key task was to provide frontline units with weapons, equipment, ammunition and gear in the necessary quantities and shortest timeframes.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters published this as a concrete wartime directive from Putin to the industrial base.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and tied to execution of the war program.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct; this is Putin personally tasking the industrial base under wartime conditions.
contrary_evidence: The article is an exhortation, not proof that the required quantities were actually delivered on schedule.

evidence.claim: Putin ordered creation of a government commission, a national strategy to 2030 and 2035, procurement plans, certification rules, specialist training, and airspace integration for unmanned aircraft systems.
evidence.title: Instructions on developing unmanned aircraft systems
evidence.excerpt: Putin ordered creation of a government commission, a national strategy to 2030 and 2035, procurement plans, certification rules, specialist training, and airspace integration for unmanned aircraft systems.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official presidential instructions with a detailed implementation architecture, timelines, and institutional owners.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022, showing late-year institutionalisation of a war-and-industrial priority.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct; the instructions were Putin's and assigned to government, ministries, security agencies, and the central bank for follow-through.
contrary_evidence: This is a planning and institution-building directive; 2022 alone does not show how fully the system executed it.

unresolved_gaps: Direct evidence on command-and-control discipline, custody, accident-prevention, and other nuclear safety procedures in 2022 is thin.
Direct evidence on expert governance and risk institutions is weak relative to the rhetoric and escalation evidence.
The package needs better household and distribution evidence, not just macro stabilization and state-budget outcomes.
Direct evidence that appointments and institutions translated into durable productivity investment is still thin.
Direct 2022 delivery evidence for health, education, housing, and food security inside Russia remains thin.
Implementation and take-up by region and group are not well documented.
Direct documentary proof of Putin's personal beneficial ownership, asset control, or hidden conflicts remains limited.
The appointment and accountability map is still too thin for a fully rounded honesty judgment.
Direct 2022 implementation metrics for procurement, output, and battlefield effectiveness remain thin.
The package still needs a cleaner separation between frantic adaptation, temporary stabilization, and genuinely effective goal advancement.
